title: RNA and cell free miRNA in one family of Kallmann's syndrome
description: Kallmann Syndrome (KS) is a rare human genetic disorder characterized by the hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with the reduction or absence of olfactory sense. The mutations on the multiple genes including Chemokine Prokineticin-2 (PROK2) were considered to contribute to the abnormal migration of gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) neurons in embryonic stage. Here, we submit RNA-seq of the peripheral blood and the cell free miRNA-seq in the serum of one family, in which the KS patient has the same mutation of PROK2 (c.223-4C>A) with his mother, and the genetic phenotype of his father is normal. The sexual development and function of his parents are normal.

samples.title: K_cell free miRNA-seq
samples.description: Protocols: 4 ml peripheral blood were harvested from three people for RNA-seq and cell-free miRNA-seq. 2 ml was added 12 ml red blood cell lysis buffer (Sangon Biotech, Shanghai, China) with fully mixing and incubated for 5 min, followed by 4000 rpm for 3 min.The precipitation collected as the leukocytes were washed by PBS for twice. Total RNA of leukocytes were extracted using Trizol (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, USA). Cell-free miRNA was extracted using miRNeasy Serum/Plasma Advanced Kit (Qiagen, Hilden, German) according to the manufacturer’s protocol. 2 μg of RNA in cell groups of different treatment condition were used for library preparation by NEBNext Ultra Directional RNA Library Prep Kit for Illumina (NEB, Ipswich, USA) following manufacturer’s recommendations.
